### AdCP 3.3 release status and GA readiness
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** The 3.3.0-beta.3 release (since succeeded by later betas, with SDKs reported on beta.4) adds experimental features across accounts, buys, creative, signals, reporting and inventory. Interop changes include a protocol envelope on every response and closed schemas staying closed within 3.x, enforced in CI. Several features were withdrawn and deferred to 4.0. The working group is tracking GA criteria: SDK alignment, green storyboards, closed-schema triage PRs awaiting consent, and a docs refresh after triage. A maintainer's open list heading into the weekend covers DOOH, enum replacements, reporting, and a 3.2.x governance backport, each waiting on reviewer approval.
- **Related:** #8736, #8915, #8793, #8149, #8980
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BK148CLU/p1793456118493969, https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BK148CLU/p1794605247121259, https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BK148CLU/p1793989289197729

### Versioning rules and cross-release translation in SDKs
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** A proposal to make cross-release translation in SDKs normative drew an objection to all three of its items, with an alternative set of versioning rules offered instead. A concession has been posted proposing adoption of the alternative's three rules for the rest of 3.x and all of 4.x, including that a minor release only adds and only to open schemas, and that replacing a field means adding a new one. The working group agenda lists confirming this as a decision item, with 4.0 planning to follow.
- **Related:** #8519, #8704, #8600, #8501
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BK148CLU/p1793989289197729

### Campaign governance documentation coherence
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** A review of the campaign-governance docs found multiple contradictions between task pages, the audit-trail and safety-model pages, the specification, and the schemas, plus several behaviors every governance agent must implement that remain undefined. Examples include inconsistent handling of a budget cut below committed spend, tension between audit mode always approving and human-review-required plans having to escalate, and a schema that rejects a case the prose says agents should accept. Issues were filed against the spec repo and the Python SDK repo.
- **Related:** #8733
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09NUQS93DF/p1793805096456139

### Averaged daily budget targets versus hard caps
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** A contributor proposed drafting a small acceptance matrix covering discovery through authorization and readback for replacing a hard daily cap with an averaged target. The proposal holds that existing constraint-relaxation rules should be preserved and that the accepted averaging window and timezone should be explicit on readback.
- **Related:** #8685
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BK148CLU/p1793645362619399

### Version pinning and capability discovery in 3.3 beta SDK readers
- **Status:** active
- **Summary:** An implementer reported that a beta-based reader pinned its capabilities call to a prerelease version, received a version-unsupported error from a seller supporting only 3.0, and failed instead of retrying unpinned. The 3.3 beta guidance says prerelease pins should only be sent to peers advertising that exact value and never negotiate down, so buyers should retry unpinned on that error; the stable SDK already does so. The thread also notes that capabilities discovery is expected to be readable without credentials, which matters for sellers who lock down authentication.
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09J28K9K29/p1794418915773829

### Synthetic population-model approach to audience signals
- **Status:** parked
- **Summary:** A member suggested evaluating a fully synthetic alternative to ID-based audience matching, where buyers plan reach and frequency on a large population model and pass virtual IDs to sellers, who map their audiences to them. The claimed benefits are removing match-rate and consent-state problems, with a neutral party supplying the model. A follow-up agreed this could be a good candidate for a dedicated working group.
- **Thread:** https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BF378H8A/p1793902771260599, https://agenticads.slack.com/archives/C09BF378H8A/p1793913489046689
